title: Pure vowels: ε and ο
learn: Learn to keep ε and ο pure

text.american: Greek has five vowel sounds, and each is pure: the mouth holds still from start to end. English slides. Your “day” starts at e and slides up to ee, your “go” starts at o and slides to oo; said that way, ε drifts toward ι and ο toward ου, which are other Greek vowels. And English blurs a vowel that is not stressed to “uh”, like the a of “about”. Greek never does: every vowel keeps its sound, stressed or not.
text.british: Greek has five vowel sounds, and each is pure: the mouth holds still from start to end. English slides. Your “day” starts at e and slides up to ee, and your “go” starts at the uh of “about” and slides to oo; said that way, ε drifts toward ι, and ο loses its round start. And English blurs a vowel that is not stressed to “uh”, like the a of “about”. Greek never does: every vowel keeps its sound, stressed or not.

text.american: Say “pet” and hold the e, with no slide: that is ε, and αι, which sounds the same. For ο, say “or” and stop before the r, short: that is ο, and ω, which sounds the same. Say “day” and “go” in a mirror and watch the jaw move at the end; then say ε and ο with the jaw still.
text.british: Say “pet” and hold the e, with no slide: that is ε, and αι, which sounds the same. For ο, say “lot” with your lips a little rounder: that is ο, and ω, which sounds the same. Say “day” and “go” in a mirror and watch the jaw and lips move at the end; then say ε and ο with them still.

steps.text: Listen to ε and ο held still in every syllable, the unstressed ones too: ὄνομα has three full vowels, and so has ἔχομεν. Not one slides, and not one goes to “uh”.

Each pair differs only in a vowel. If your ε slides toward ee, ἕνα becomes ἵνα and βασιλέα, king, becomes βασιλεία, kingdom; if your ο slides toward oo, ὅσα becomes οὖσα. Hear both words, then say both, holding each vowel still.
Say each word after the voice, with your jaw still on every vowel. Give the vowels that are not stressed their full sound too: ἀγάπη starts with a full a, not “uh”.

God is love: this verse is full of ε and ο, each ε, αι, ο and ω marked. Hear it, then say it with every vowel held still. Where ε or ο stands in a pair, ει, οι or ου, the pair has its own sound instead, ee, ee or oo.
